newsitem.title: USA: Judge denies suppressing British nanny statements.
newsitem.headline: Judge denies suppressing British nanny statements.

text.p: A jury will hear statements a 19-year-old British nanny made to police that she tossed around and dropped on the floor a 9-month-old infant she is accused of killing, a judge ruled on Friday.
Massachusetts Superior Court Judge Hiller Zobel denied a motion filed by the nanny's lawyers to have the statements suppressed on the grounds they were coerced by police.

British au pair Louise Woodward told police shortly after the infant, Matthew Eappen, was hospitalized that she "dropped the baby on the floor" and "tossed the baby on the bed" and "may have been a little rough with the baby."

Though police informed Woodward of her constitutional right to remain silent, her lawyers said that the officers also told her that doctors wanted information about what happened to the baby in the hours before he was admitted to Boston's Children's Hospital.
Woodward, who arrived in the United States in June and began working for the Eappen family in November, has pleaded not guilty to first-degree murder charges.
The case has generated anger in Britain because of the severity of the charges and the judge's refusal to have her released on bail.

Woodward called rescue workers to her employers' home in February and told them the boy had suddenly stopped breathing. She is alleged to have killed the infant in February by severely shaking him and striking his head on a hard surface, causing a skull fracture.
If convicted of first-degree murder, she would face a mandatory life sentence with no eligibility for parole.
The trial is scheduled to begin in July.
